sentences.text: on 8 October, 2025
The Honourable Sri Justice J. Sreenivas Rao

Criminal Petition No.770 of 2021
Order:

This Criminal Petition has been filed by the petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 4 seeking to quash the proceeding in Crime.No.49 of 2021 of Jawahar Nagar Police Station, Rachakonda Commissionerate,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 468 and 471 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code (In short 'IPC').
2.

entities.text: Jawahar Nagar Police Station, Rachakonda Commissionerate
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Heard Mr.K.Mohan, learned counsel for the petitioner, Mr.M.Srinivas Rao, learned counsel for respondent No.2 and Mr.M.Vivekanand Reddy, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1-State.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners have not committed any offence and they were falsely implicated in the present crime.

He further submitted that there are civil disputes between the petitioners and respondent No.2 filed a suit in O.S.No.13 of 2021 before the learned XVI Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy at Malkajgiri, and the same is pending.

entities.text: XVI Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The allegations made against the petitioners in the complaint would clearly reveal that they are civil in nature and hence the continuation of proceedings against the petitioners is a clear abuse of the process of law.

4. Per Contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 submitted that there are specific allegations levelled against the petitioners to attract the ingredients under Sections 420, 468 and 471 read with Section 34 of IPC.

Whether the petitioners have committed the offence or not, have to be revealed after full-fledged trial and the petitioners are not entitled to seek quashing of the proceedings in Crime No.49 of 2021.
5.

Learned counsel for the petitioner by way of reply submitted that this Court on 02.10.2021, while ordering notice before admission, directed the Investigating Officer to conduct investigation after following the due procedure as contemplated under Section 41-A of Cr.P.C.

He further submitted that as on today the investigation has not been completed and requested this Court to direct the Investigating Officer to follow the procedure as contemplated under Section 41-A of Cr.P.C and also guidelines formulated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar 1.
6. The said submission has not opposed by learned counsel for respondent No.2.
7.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Taking into consideration the above said submissions made by the respective parties, and without expressing any view on merits of the case, the Investigating Officer is directed to follow the procedure prescribed under Section 41-A Cr.P.C./Section 35 of BNSS and the guidelines formulated Sri. G.V. Gyaneshwar Naidu vs The State Of Telangana And Another on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146901413/
1 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Arnesh Kumar supra.

entities.text: G.V. Gyaneshwar Naidu vs The State Of Telangana And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. It is made clear that the petitioners shall cooperate with the Investigating Officer for the investigation and make themselves available to him as and when required and also provide the information/documents as sought by him to conclude the investigation.

If the petitioners fail to cooperate with the Investigating Officer for investigation, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to take action against them in accordance with law.
10.
Subject to the above directions, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous applications, if any, pending in this petition stand closed.
